title: Understanding the IMO Regulatory System for Executives
audience: Leaders of maritime administrations, ports and shipping companies, and senior managers without a legal background
learning_outcome: Map regulatory decision-making and separate the responsibilities of international and national bodies
capstone: A one-page map of regulatory sources and management decisions

sessions.title: The legal and institutional structure of the maritime sector
sessions.detail: IMO, ILO, the Member State and the national maritime administration; the limits of each body's competence
sessions.deliverable: Identify the responsible body for three hypothetical issues

sessions.title: IMO committees and the path to a decision
sessions.detail: Assembly, Council, MSC, MEPC, LEG, FAL; the III and HTW Sub-Committees
sessions.deliverable: A diagram of how an issue is adopted and followed up

sessions.title: International instruments and their legal standing
sessions.detail: Convention, code, resolution, circular and guidance; an overview of SOLAS, MARPOL, STCW and FAL
sessions.deliverable: A table classifying instruments and responsibilities

sessions.title: Regulatory intelligence and reporting to the board
sessions.detail: Tracking regulatory change, entry into force, implementation owners, timing and risk

hook: When a maritime requirement comes up, a manager needs to know exactly which instrument and which authority it rests on.
problem: Confusion about the competence of IMO, ILO and national authorities, and mixing binding requirements with guidance.
method: Analysis of three management problems, classification of instruments and a regulatory report to the board.
editorial_questions: How do we distinguish the roles of IMO, ILO and the Member State?
Is every IMO resolution or guideline binding on our organisation?
How do we report a regulatory change to the board as a short decision?
measurable_outcomes: Identify the correct authority and instrument for three organisational issues
Classify, with reasons, whether an instrument is binding and whom it covers
Prepare a one-page map of issue, source, national owner and proposed action
hypothetical_case: The maritime administration of the fictional State of Aban receives three letters at once: on seafarer certificates, the maritime single window and crew working conditions. Participants must identify the authority, the instrument and the national decision point for each.
scientific_note: The course builds regulatory literacy for managers. Its analysis does not replace a State's official legal interpretation or the competence of a certifying authority.

title: From IMO Regulation to National Implementation
audience: Policymakers and managers in maritime administrations, and inspectors working at policy level
learning_outcome: Assess the implementation gap for an international obligation and propose a roadmap
capstone: A gap assessment matrix and implementation roadmap

sessions.title: Sources of obligation and scope of application
sessions.detail: Identifying binding instruments, membership, reservations and dates of application; checking the State and the type of activity

sessions.title: The III Code and State responsibility
sessions.detail: The common part and the duties of flag, coastal and port States; separating responsibilities

sessions.title: Diagnosing implementation gaps
sessions.detail: Evidence on laws, processes, competences, inspection and monitoring
sessions.deliverable: A matrix of current status and gaps

sessions.title: Turning obligations into regulations and procedures
sessions.detail: The chain from obligation to statute, regulation and working procedure; stakeholders
sessions.deliverable: A map of the regulatory reform package

sessions.title: Governing implementation and managing change
sessions.detail: Budget, capacity building, data, oversight, reporting and organisational resistance

sessions.title: Integrated exercise: assessing a fictional State
sessions.detail: Prioritising action by risk, urgency and feasibility

hook: International obligations only take effect once they are translated into national responsibility and action.
problem: The gap between acceding to IMO instruments and the processes, powers and evidence of national implementation.
method: A III Code workshop, institutional diagnosis and the design of a RACI and reform roadmap.
editorial_questions: At which layer does the gap between international obligation and national implementation appear?
How are the roles of flag, coastal and port State documented?
Which gaps must be closed in the first 90 days?
measurable_outcomes: List the applicable obligations, specifying the version and scope
Assess gaps in law, process, organisational capacity and oversight on the basis of evidence
Prepare a time-bound roadmap and RACI matrix
hypothetical_case: A fictional maritime administration has scattered laws, inconsistent inspection processes and unclear allocation of responsibility. Groups must classify the evidence and prepare a reform package to present to management.
scientific_note: The III Code and the IMSAS audit scheme must be considered in light of the binding instruments that apply to each State. The course is not an official IMO audit.

title: Port Governance for Senior Managers
audience: Port authority managers, terminal operators and policy managers
learning_outcome: Choose a governance model and a performance monitoring structure that fit the port's problem
capstone: A port governance diagnostic and KPI dashboard

sessions.title: Port governance models
sessions.detail: Service, tool and landlord ports; the responsibilities of the State and the private sector

sessions.title: The institutional map and conflicting roles
sessions.detail: Separating regulator, owner and operator; accountability, powers and conflicts of interest
sessions.deliverable: A chart of roles and decision rights

sessions.title: Performance and indicators
sessions.detail: Operational, financial and institutional performance; the limits of the CPPI

sessions.title: Governing concession agreements
sessions.detail: Asset ownership, monitoring obligations, operating rights, review and oversight

sessions.title: Designing reform and managing change
sessions.detail: The cycle of diagnosis, choice, implementation, monitoring and feedback; stakeholder communication

sessions.title: Case workshop: a fictional port
sessions.detail: Balancing efficiency, competition, public interest and accountability
sessions.deliverable: A proposal package for the board

hook: A port's governance model is a question of accountability before it is a question of ownership.
problem: Overlap between regulation, ownership and operation, and weak oversight of concessions and performance indicators.
method: Comparison of port models, a case study of institutional reform and the design of a KPI dashboard.
editorial_questions: How do the service, tool and landlord models fit a particular port?
Where are the boundaries between regulator, owner and operator?
Which indicators measure the balance between efficiency and public interest?
measurable_outcomes: Compare governance models and the risks of role conflict
Define decision rights and performance indicators for a fictional port
Propose an institutional reform package and a management dashboard
hypothetical_case: The fictional port of Sepehr faces falling terminal productivity and a conflict between its regulatory and operating roles. Teams must make a reasoned choice between three governance models.
scientific_note: The models in the World Bank Port Reform Toolkit are analytical tools and policy guidance, not treaty obligations.

title: Maritime Contracts, Tenders and Procurement
audience: Legal, procurement, contract and port managers
learning_outcome: Identify contractual risks and design controls for the procurement process
capstone: A risk matrix and RFP checklist

sessions.title: The contractual framework and types of instrument
sessions.detail: Commercial contracts, charter parties, concessions, MoUs and the use of BIMCO forms
sessions.deliverable: A map for choosing the contractual instrument

sessions.title: Designing the RFP and tender requirements
sessions.detail: Scope, evaluation criteria, transparency, conflicts of interest, documents and outputs

sessions.title: Risk and the allocation of responsibility
sessions.detail: Regulatory risk, change in law, delay, performance, force majeure, insurance and guarantees

sessions.title: Procurement controls and corporate governance
sessions.detail: Approvals, documentation, confidentiality and control points

sessions.title: Negotiation and dispute prevention
sessions.detail: Clear wording of key clauses, change control, notices and dispute resolution
sessions.deliverable: Proposed revisions to five hypothetical clauses

sessions.title: Workshop: assessing a fictional contract
sessions.detail: Review of a mock contract with stated assumptions
sessions.deliverable: A management note on contract risk

hook: A good contract does not hide risk; it makes risk something you can decide on before you sign.
problem: Unclear tender scope, risk allocation and mechanisms for managing change and disputes.
method: Review of a sample RFP, analysis of key clauses and a risk allocation matrix.
editorial_questions: Which type of contractual instrument fits the problem?
How can the risks of change in law, delay and performance be allocated fairly?
Where are the control points for transparency and dispute management?
measurable_outcomes: Choose the contract type and RFP structure that fit the need
Design a risk allocation matrix and conflict-of-interest controls
Propose redrafts of five high-risk clauses for specialist review and negotiation
hypothetical_case: A fictional port employer has received a draft tender with vague evaluation criteria and unbalanced change-in-law clauses. Groups must list the risks and the changes they propose.
scientific_note: BIMCO standard forms do not replace local legal advice or a review of whether specific clauses are enforceable in a given contract.

title: STCW and Seafarer Administration for Policymakers
audience: Maritime administrations, training centres and maritime human resources managers
learning_outcome: Analyse the requirements for administering certificates and assuring the quality of seafarer training
capstone: A compliance matrix and plan to improve the quality system

sessions.title: The structure of the STCW Convention and Code
sessions.detail: Articles of the Convention, mandatory Part A and guidance in Part B; the concept of competence
sessions.deliverable: A table of the hierarchy of requirements

sessions.title: Issuing, recognising and verifying certificates
sessions.detail: Competent bodies, verification, documents and oversight responsibility
sessions.deliverable: A map of the certificate cycle

sessions.title: Quality assurance of maritime training centres
sessions.detail: Competence-based curricula, assessment, independent evaluation and quality

sessions.title: MLC 2006 and the human element
sessions.detail: The roles of IMO and ILO; working conditions, welfare, hours of work and complaints
sessions.deliverable: A map linking STCW and MLC

sessions.title: Changing technology and new skills
sessions.detail: The comprehensive STCW review, alternative fuels and competence needs analysis
sessions.deliverable: A list of competence development needs

sessions.title: Case study: reforming a training system
sessions.detail: Gap analysis of a fictional training centre
sessions.deliverable: A reform plan with monitoring indicators

hook: The credibility of certificates and the quality of seafarer training depend on a sound system of oversight.
problem: Gaps in issuing and verifying certificates, in training centre quality assurance and in the boundary between STCW and MLC.
method: Analysis of the quality system and certificate cycle, and a workshop assessing a training centre.
editorial_questions: What different legal standing do Parts A and B of the STCW Code have?
How are certificate issue, recognition and verification controlled?
What role does the MLC play alongside STCW?
measurable_outcomes: Separate the structure of STCW requirements and the competent authority
Identify risks in a certification system and assess the quality of a training centre
Propose a plan to reform the quality system and monitor performance
hypothetical_case: The fictional training centre Daryadan faces complaints about training quality, weak assessment records and delays in verifying certificates.
scientific_note: This policy and management course does not replace a professional competence course for seafarers under STCW, or approval of training by the competent State.

title: International Maritime Negotiation Masterclass
audience: International affairs managers, heads of negotiating delegations and senior managers
learning_outcome: Prepare a negotiation strategy and carry out a documented role play
capstone: A delegation briefing book and the record of a simulation

sessions.title: The structure of international negotiation
sessions.detail: Interests versus positions, objectives, BATNA, red lines and constraints
sessions.deliverable: A sheet of negotiating objectives and limits

sessions.title: Stakeholder maps and coalitions
sessions.detail: Influence and interest analysis, the negotiating team and agenda management

sessions.title: Preparing the delegation
sessions.detail: The briefing book, key messages, members' roles, formal language and recording decisions

sessions.title: First simulation: a multilateral meeting
sessions.detail: Role play on a fictional scenario to amend requirements
sessions.deliverable: A record of proposals and points of agreement

sessions.title: Drafting text and negotiating clauses
sessions.detail: Drafting a memorandum of understanding or position paper and resolving conflicts
sessions.deliverable: A first draft of the agreed text

sessions.title: Second simulation and feedback
sessions.detail: A repeat negotiation, structured feedback and post-meeting commitments

hook: Professional international negotiation starts with a documented position, a coordinated team and a way to follow up.
problem: Entering negotiations without a stakeholder map, a clear delegation mandate or proposed text.
method: Building a briefing book, multilateral role play and practice in drafting agreed text.
editorial_questions: How do we move from stated positions to the parties' real interests?
How are a coalition map, BATNA and red lines prepared?
How are minutes and agreed text recorded without ambiguity?
measurable_outcomes: Prepare a negotiation strategy and briefing book
Carry out the delegation's role and messages in a multilateral simulation
Draft an agreement and a measurable follow-up plan
hypothetical_case: Delegations from three fictional States negotiate a new framework for cooperation on port safety. Each delegation has different interests, budget constraints and opening text.
scientific_note: The negotiation scenario is fictional and no position is attributed to any real government or organisation.

title: Managing International Maritime Cooperation
audience: International relations managers in government bodies and associations
learning_outcome: Design a cooperation programme that can be implemented and evaluated
capstone: A cooperation matrix and a draft non-binding MoU

sessions.title: Types of international cooperation
sessions.detail: Bilateral, multilateral, institutional, research and capacity-building cooperation; the risk of dependency

sessions.title: From need to the right partner
sessions.detail: Assessing strategic fit, the parties' capacity and shared interests

sessions.title: The MoU framework and its governance
sessions.detail: Subject, scope, points of contact, confidentiality, disputes, responsibility and monitoring
sessions.deliverable: A draft of the main MoU clauses

sessions.title: Implementing cooperation and accountability
sessions.detail: Action plan, KPIs, meeting arrangements, transparency and risk management

hook: Successful international cooperation has to go beyond the memorandum and gain an owner, a timetable and indicators.
problem: Choosing partners without screening, and signing MoUs without a monitoring framework or a division of commitments.
method: Partner assessment, drafting an MoU and designing a six-month programme.
editorial_questions: Which model of cooperation fits the organisation's real problem?
How is a foreign partner screened on its capacity to deliver?
How can an MoU and action plan be made measurable?
measurable_outcomes: Score cooperation opportunities by value and feasibility
Prepare a partner screening matrix for the options
Design a draft non-binding MoU and a six-month action plan
hypothetical_case: A fictional port organisation has received three proposals for cooperation on training, data and performance improvement. Participants must choose the preferred partner.
scientific_note: Whether an MoU is binding depends on its final text, the parties' intention and the applicable legal system, and must be checked.

title: Board Briefing on Maritime Decarbonization Regulation
audience: Boards, chief executives, compliance managers and policymakers
learning_outcome: Separate adopted policy from proposals under negotiation and prioritise risk
capstone: A decision brief on three regulatory scenarios

sessions.title: The map of maritime climate regulation
sessions.detail: MARPOL Annex VI, the 2023 IMO Strategy and the difference between targets and requirements

sessions.title: Regional regulation and its scope
sessions.detail: EU ETS for shipping and FuelEU Maritime; effects on contracts and operations
sessions.deliverable: An exposure matrix for the organisation

sessions.title: Board decision scenarios
sessions.detail: The uncertain status of the IMO Net-Zero Framework, three scenarios and no-regret actions

hook: In maritime climate regulation, the difference between approval, final adoption and entry into force is the basis of investment decisions.
problem: Decisions based on unfinished drafts, or regional rules wrongly generalised.
method: An EU ETS and FuelEU scope matrix, three scenarios and a board decision note.
editorial_questions: Which climate obligations are binding now, and which are strategies or proposals?
What exposure do the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime create for operations?
How should a board decide in the face of uncertainty over the IMO Net-Zero Framework?
measurable_outcomes: Place the legal status and dates of climate instruments on a timeline
Prepare a matrix of the organisation's exposure to global and regional rules
Weigh three scenarios and no-regret actions in a decision brief
hypothetical_case: A fictional shipping company must decide on fleet renewal and a fuel supply contract. Three regulatory scenarios with different degrees of uncertainty are examined.
scientific_note: As of 25 October 2026, the IMO Net-Zero Framework is not presented as finally adopted or in force. The state of negotiations must be checked again before publication or delivery.

title: Maritime Digitalization & Single Window Governance
audience: Maritime administrations, ports and digital transformation managers
learning_outcome: Design a data governance map and an organisational plan for implementing a maritime single window

sessions.title: The FAL requirement and ship arrival and departure
sessions.detail: The purpose and scope of the MSW and information exchange processes
sessions.deliverable: A list of data and stakeholders

sessions.title: Data responsibility and inter-agency exchange
sessions.detail: Data ownership, quality, consent, confidentiality and exchange

sessions.title: Cyber security from a governance perspective
sessions.detail: Board decisions and the separate role of technical security specialists
sessions.deliverable: A governance risk register for security

sessions.title: A digitalisation roadmap
sessions.detail: Service priorities, acceptance criteria, indicators and change management

hook: A maritime single window is not just software; it is an agreement between agencies about data and responsibility.
problem: Parallel systems, repeated data entry and no governance across the port, customs and other agencies.
method: Designing the data flow, a responsibility matrix and a maritime single window roadmap.
editorial_questions: How does a maritime single window differ from a port community system and a customs single window?
Who owns the data and who manages exchange between agencies?
Which criteria show that the MSW has been delivered?
measurable_outcomes: Analyse the scope of the MSW and the FAL requirements at organisational level
Design a matrix of agencies' responsibilities and data exchange
Write a governance roadmap for digitalisation and cyber risk control
hypothetical_case: A fictional port has six separate portals for ship arrival information, and the same data is entered several times. Groups must propose a governance design for a single point of data entry and exchange between agencies.
scientific_note: The FAL amendments on the MSW have been in force since 1 January 2024. Determining the obligation and its enforcement for a particular State requires checking its membership and national law.

title: Port Investment, PPP & Concession Governance
audience: Port managers, public contracting authorities, investors and developers
learning_outcome: Make an initial assessment of the institutional structure and risks of a port PPP project

sessions.title: Partnership and governance models
sessions.detail: Service contracts, concessions and PPPs, and how they differ from full privatisation
sessions.deliverable: A decision tree for choosing a model

sessions.title: Stakeholders and institutional bankability
sessions.detail: Clarity of permits, the authority's competence, tariff regulation and conflicts of interest

sessions.title: Risk structure and concession monitoring
sessions.detail: Risk allocation and contractual indicators under port oversight

sessions.title: Workshop: a fictional project
sessions.detail: Comparing two transaction structures and presenting to an investment committee

hook: The bankability of a port project starts with clear powers, risks and oversight arrangements.
problem: Choosing an unsuitable public-private partnership model, and the regulatory risks of concession agreements.
method: Screening partnership models, institutional due diligence and defending an investment option.
editorial_questions: How does a PPP differ from a concession and a service contract?
How does institutional risk affect a project's bankability?
Which oversight indicators and review mechanisms are needed?
measurable_outcomes: Compare two transaction models in terms of public interest and oversight capacity
Prepare an institutional due diligence and risk matrix
Write a decision note on the concession structure for an investment committee
hypothetical_case: A fictional port is choosing between an operating concession and an investment partnership to develop a container terminal. The assumptions on demand and oversight differ.
scientific_note: The assessment is preliminary and institutional. It is not a bankable financial feasibility study or a definitive investment recommendation.

title: Independent Expert & Maritime Dispute Advisory
audience: Contract managers, industry advisers and collaborating lawyers
learning_outcome: Recognise the role of impartial expertise and its technical and legal limits

sessions.title: Independence, conflicts of interest and the limits of the mandate
sessions.detail: Terms of reference for industry analysis compared with advocacy and acting as an expert witness
sessions.deliverable: A checklist for accepting an assignment

sessions.title: The structure of an expert report
sessions.detail: Claims, evidence, assumptions, limitations and reviewability
sessions.deliverable: An outline of an expert report

sessions.title: Document review and dispute prevention
sessions.detail: A timeline of claims, contractual issues and non-judicial options
sessions.deliverable: A table of disputed issues and evidence

hook: Independent expertise is valuable when the question, the evidence and the limits of the analysis are transparent.
problem: An unclear mandate for the expert and poor documentation of disputes under maritime contracts.
method: An independence checklist, a report structure and a timeline of claims and documents.
editorial_questions: How does an independent expert differ from a lawyer and an expert witness?
What must be disclosed before accepting an assignment?
How does an expert report remain reviewable and impartial?
measurable_outcomes: Assess independence and conflicts of interest
Prepare a report structure with data, assumptions and limitations stated openly
Organise a list of issues and a timeline of the evidence in a dispute
hypothetical_case: A dispute has arisen between a fictional port employer and a contractor over delays in commissioning equipment. Groups must separate claims from evidence and write down the technical question that can be examined.
scientific_note: This module does not replace legal representation, arbitration or the formal opinion of an expert appointed by a court.

title: Train-the-Trainer & Quality Assurance
audience: Lecturers at maritime training centres and in-house trainers
learning_outcome: Design, pilot and evaluate a competence-based training unit
capstone: A lesson pack and micro-teaching assessment

sessions.title: Backward design from outcomes
sessions.detail: Audience, behavioural objectives, evidence of learning and pass criteria
sessions.deliverable: A map aligning objectives and assessment

sessions.title: Building a reliable lesson pack
sessions.detail: Primary sources first, versions of instruments, citation and common biases

sessions.title: Active learning and assessment tools
sessions.detail: Case studies, simulation, rubrics, feedback and accessibility

sessions.title: Pilot teaching and review
sessions.detail: A 20-minute delivery, peer assessment and the final version

hook: Specialist knowledge stays in an organisation when it can be taught, assessed and reviewed.
problem: Dependence on a few trainers, vague lesson objectives and assessments that cannot be measured.
method: Backward design, rubrics, a 20-minute pilot lesson and peer review.
editorial_questions: How is a behavioural objective linked to evidence of learning?
How are the accuracy and version of reference instruments checked?
What evidence of quality does pilot teaching provide?
measurable_outcomes: Design behavioural objectives and a consistent rubric
Review a lesson pack against primary sources, versions and legal status
Deliver a lesson pack and a 20-minute pilot lesson
hypothetical_case: A fictional lesson pack is presented with outdated instruments, vague objectives and an unrelated test. Teams revise it and deliver a short lesson.
scientific_note: The train-the-trainer course is an internal training quality programme. On its own it does not create a licence or competence to teach STCW courses.
